- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward with greater magnitude.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +0.5–1.0 in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot in 3–7 day horizon; apply smoothing or lag correction.
- Mean reversion is evident in 10–14 day horizon: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.1–0.3; if below, raise by 0.1–0.3.
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses late-stage momentum (last 5–7 days of true outcome); anchor forecast to last 7–10 days of history for final 10–15 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.10) and history shows no clear trend, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply slight upward bias to avoid underestimation.
